text.title: Consistency and Standards Worked Example
text.summary: One end-to-end worked example of Consistency and Standards producing a valid spec artefact, anonymised for portability. Plus canonical visual, functional, and verbal pattern examples and platform reference examples.

step.name: trigger
step.text: Engagement onboarded; the Consistency and Standards methodology was selected after Applies-If was satisfied (named owner Ruslan Faion, downstream consumer named in engagement charter, source-of-truth pinned in docs/).

step.name: apply-rules
step.text: Walked the rules from 01-core-rules.xml. Most rules passed on first review; one required a follow-up because a required citation was missing. Captured the gap, patched, re-ran.

step.name: produce
step.text: Filled templates/consistency-standards.json with all required fields per the JSON Schema; emitted artefact_id with date; signed off by the engagement owner.

step.name: validate
step.text: Ran scripts/validate-consistency-standards.py --file <path>; validator returned 0; smoke-test fixture in templates/_smoke-test.json also passed.

step.name: handover
step.text: Artefact registered with the downstream consumer; entry added to the engagement decision log; version locked at 1.1.0.

example.note: Primary action: always #0066CC. Destructive action: always #CC0000. Success: always #00CC66. Warning: always #FFCC00. Spacing base unit: 8px; all margins are multiples (8, 16, 24, 32).
Logo click always goes to home. Back button always goes to previous page. Search always in top area. Single click selects; double click opens/edits.
Create (not Add/New/Insert). Delete (not Remove/Trash/Erase). Edit (not Modify/Change/Update). Save (not Store/Apply/Confirm). Success (not Done/Complete/OK). Error (not Failed/Problem/Issue).

iOS: Back button always top-left, swipe from edge to go back, pull to refresh, tab bar at bottom. These conventions are so reliable that deviating from any of them generates App Store reviews specifically calling out the inconsistency.
Google products share search pattern, account menu, iconography across Gmail, Drive, Calendar, and Maps — users transfer knowledge between products without relearning.

text.example: Applies-If held → inputs reachable → rules walked → artefact filled → validator returned 0 → owner signed off → downstream consumer registered.
